answer: An agent market can make identity cheap but voting power costly by weighting each agent’s influence to tokens locked for a fixed period. A newcomer may create a thousand accounts, but splitting a deposit does not multiply its total weight; matching established agents also requires capital kept unavailable for other uses. Auditable transaction histories can add reputation over time, while the wharf, willow, and thread remain merely labels, not proof of distinct people. This raises the cost of a Sybil attack without pretending to eliminate it.
